failure_patterns.pattern: endpoint_selection: Some calls used an endpoint that did not best match the requested capability, fanned one item out across unrelated catalogs, or named an endpoint absent from the available tools.

rejected_edits.content: - Include an optional parameter whenever it directly encodes a requested facet, even if the user phrases it in prose or the endpoint has a default. For the first N results from a paginated endpoint, set page to 1 and the supported limit or per-page parameter to N, even when page 1 is implied rather than stated. For an unfiltered, random, or full/standard result, use a documented “all” or unfiltered selector when needed to preserve that scope. Do not add options that are neither requested nor needed to express it, or invent values. For missing required values, use only a documented default or a value unambiguously derivable from the query.
rejected_edits.target: - Include an optional parameter whenever it directly encodes a requested facet, even if the user phrases it in prose or the endpoint has a default. For an unfiltered, random, or full/standard result, use a documented “all” or unfiltered selector when needed to preserve that scope. Do not add options that are neither requested nor needed to express it, or invent values. For missing required values, use only a documented default or a value unambiguously derivable from the query.

rejected_edits.content: - If the response contract specifies an ordering (for example, sorting calls by tool name), reorder the call objects to match it after selecting and validating the calls; do not simply preserve query order.

- Treat every explicitly described action and requested detail as part of the task, including steps narrated as background or a sequence; count an operation as already completed only when the prompt supplies its result or explicitly says not to repeat it. Make a checklist with one entry per desired result and its requested facets, and verify that each is covered by an appropriate call.
- For each checklist item, shortlist only endpoints whose documented capability returns the requested kind of result for that resource or category. Use the exact full tool identifier from the available-tools list and follow its documented schema. Choose the single best-supported endpoint unless the user explicitly requests multiple sources or distinct facets require separate calls. Do not substitute tangential endpoints, fan an item out across unrelated catalogs, treat suggestions as product listings, infer capabilities from a provider name, or invent an endpoint absent from the available-tools list.
rejected_edits.target: - Break the request into distinct operations and match each to an endpoint by its documented capability and parameter schema—not merely by provider or broad topic. Use the exact full tool identifier from the available-tools list. Do not substitute a tangential endpoint or call several similar alternatives for the same requested result.

rejected_edits.content: - For each call, map every requested constraint and output facet independently to its documented parameter; do not assume one filter implies another. Bind each constraint only to the call it modifies, and do not carry dates, limits, filters, or pagination across operations. Put each parameter in the required or optional list exactly as the schema classifies it: a requested filter remains optional when the endpoint marks it optional. Distinguish regional storefront hostnames from marketplace codes: if the field expects a country or region code, derive it from the supplied storefront or region; if it expects a hostname, preserve the hostname.
rejected_edits.target: - Use each endpoint's exact parameter names and required/optional placement. Bind every constraint only to the call it modifies; do not carry dates, limits, filters, or pagination across operations.
